us-20261123-news-1.title: ¿Se acabó la división? Lo que una ola demócrata en las elecciones de medio término podría significar para los precios, los aranceles y el presupuesto

segments.src: Early reports indicate that Democrats have won control of both the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterm elections, with frustration over the cost of living cited as a central theme among voters.
segments.tr: Los primeros informes indican que los demócratas han ganado el control tanto de la Cámara de Representantes como del Senado en las elecciones de medio término de 2026, citando la frustración por el costo de vida como un tema central entre los votantes.

segments.src: Final tallies and certification can take weeks, so treat any single count with caution.
segments.tr: Los recuentos finales y la certificación pueden tardar semanas, por lo que cualquier recuento único debe tomarse con cautela.

segments.src: The more useful question for most households is this: **if control of Congress changes hands, what can lawmakers actually do, and what stays out of their reach?**
segments.tr: La pregunta más útil para la mayoría de los hogares es esta: **si el control del Congreso cambia de manos, ¿qué pueden hacer realmente los legisladores y qué queda fuera de su alcance?**

segments.src: This explainer walks through the constitutional tools a new Congress has, the limits it faces, and what to watch between now and the 2028 election.
segments.tr: Esta guía explicativa analiza las herramientas constitucionales que tiene un nuevo Congreso, los límites a los que se enfrenta y a qué prestar atención entre ahora y las elecciones de 2028.

segments.src: It is a look at how the system works, not an endorsement of any party or policy.
segments.tr: Es un análisis de cómo funciona el sistema, no un respaldo a ningún partido o política.

segments.src: ## The timeline: nothing changes overnight
segments.tr: ## El cronograma: nada cambia de la noche a la mañana

segments.src: A newly elected Congress is sworn in on January 3, 2027.
segments.tr: Un Congreso recién elegido jura su cargo el 3 de enero de 2027.

segments.src: Until then, the current Congress remains in office, including during any "lame-duck" session in December.
segments.tr: Hasta entonces, el Congreso actual permanece en funciones, incluso durante cualquier sesión de "pato cojo" en diciembre.

segments.src: Even after the handoff, the president keeps the executive branch, the veto pen and most day-to-day regulatory decisions.
segments.tr: Incluso después del traspaso, el presidente conserva el poder ejecutivo, el derecho de veto y la mayoría de las decisiones regulatorias cotidianas.

segments.src: That means voter anger over prices does not translate into an immediate policy shift.
segments.tr: Eso significa que la indignación de los votantes por los precios no se traduce en un cambio de política inmediato.

segments.src: Congress sets the rules and the money.
segments.tr: El Congreso establece las reglas y el dinero.

segments.src: The White House carries them out.
segments.tr: La Casa Blanca los lleva a cabo.

segments.src: ## Prices: Congress has indirect levers, not a price dial
segments.tr: ## Precios: el Congreso tiene palancas indirectas, no un dial de precios

segments.src: No branch of government can directly set the price of groceries, rent or gasoline.
segments.tr: Ninguna rama del gobierno puede fijar directamente el precio de los alimentos, el alquiler o la gasolina.

segments.src: Inflation and affordability are shaped by interest rates (set by the independent Federal Reserve), supply chains, energy markets, wages, housing supply and trade policy.
segments.tr: La inflación y la asequibilidad están determinadas por las tasas de interés (fijadas por la Reserva Federal independiente), las cadenas de suministro, los mercados energéticos, los salarios, la oferta de vivienda y la política comercial.

segments.src: What Congress can influence:
segments.tr: En lo que el Congreso puede influir:

segments.src: - **Taxes and credits.** Changes to tax law can alter what families keep, but most major tax legislation needs 60 votes in the Senate unless it moves through the budget reconciliation process.
segments.tr: - **Impuestos y créditos.** Los cambios en la ley tributaria pueden alterar lo que conservan las familias, pero la mayoría de la legislación fiscal principal necesita 60 votos en el Senado a menos que se tramite a través del proceso de reconciliación presupuestaria.

segments.src: - **Spending programs.** Funding for housing, food assistance, health subsidies and energy programs is set in law.
segments.tr: - **Programas de gasto.** La financiación para la vivienda, la asistencia alimentaria, los subsidios de salud y los programas de energía se establece por ley.

segments.src: - **Trade rules.** Tariffs are taxes on imports, and the Constitution gives Congress the power to levy them (more below).
segments.tr: - **Reglas comerciales.** Los aranceles son impuestos a las importaciones, y la Constitución otorga al Congreso la facultad de imponerlos (más adelante se detalla).

segments.src: - **Regulatory pressure.** Hearings, funding limits and statutory changes can push agencies in a different direction.
segments.tr: - **Presión regulatoria.** Las audiencias, los límites de financiación y las modificaciones legales pueden empujar a las agencias en una dirección diferente.

segments.src: What it cannot do quickly: lower mortgage rates, reverse global commodity swings or override the Fed.
segments.tr: Lo que no puede hacer rápidamente: bajar las tasas hipotecarias, revertir las oscilaciones mundiales de las materias primas o anular las decisiones de la Fed.

segments.src: Economists generally caution that policy changes take months or years to show up in household budgets.
segments.tr: Los economistas suelen advertir que los cambios de política tardan meses o años en verse reflejados en los presupuestos familiares.

segments.src: ## Tariffs: Congress holds the power on paper, but the veto looms
segments.tr: ## Aranceles: el Congreso tiene el poder en el papel, pero el veto se cierne

segments.src: Under the Constitution, the power to impose tariffs belongs to Congress.
segments.tr: Según la Constitución, la facultad de imponer aranceles le corresponde al Congreso.

segments.src: Over decades, lawmakers have delegated broad authority to the president through laws such as Section 232 (national security), Section 301 (unfair trade practices) and emergency statutes.
segments.tr: A lo largo de las décadas, los legisladores han delegado una amplia autoridad en el presidente a través de leyes como la Sección 232 (seguridad nacional), la Sección 301 (prácticas comerciales desleales) y estatutos de emergencia.

segments.src: Much of recent tariff policy has relied on those delegations, and some of them have been challenged in court.
segments.tr: Gran parte de la política arancelaria reciente se ha basado en esas delegaciones, y algunas de ellas han sido impugnadas ante los tribunales.

segments.src: A Democratic-controlled Congress could try to:
segments.tr: Un Congreso controlado por los demócratas podría intentar:

segments.src: 1. **Pass legislation** narrowing or ending specific tariff authorities.
segments.tr: 1. **Aprobar legislación** que limite o ponga fin a facultades arancelarias específicas.

segments.src: 2. **Use disapproval resolutions**, where the law provides for them, to terminate emergency declarations that underpin certain tariffs.
segments.tr: 2. **Utilizar resoluciones de desaprobación**, donde la ley lo prevea, para finalizar las declaraciones de emergencia que sustentan ciertos aranceles.

segments.src: 3. **Hold hearings** that require officials to explain costs, exemptions and effects on consumers and businesses.
segments.tr: 3. **Celebrar audiencias** que exijan a los funcionarios explicar los costos, las exenciones y los efectos sobre los consumidores y las empresas.

segments.src: 4. **Attach conditions** to must-pass legislation.
segments.tr: 4. **Añadir condiciones** a leyes de aprobación obligatoria.

segments.src: The obstacle is arithmetic.
segments.tr: El obstáculo es la aritmética.

segments.src: A president can veto a bill, and overriding a veto requires two-thirds of both chambers.
segments.tr: Un presidente puede vetar un proyecto de ley, y anular un veto requiere dos tercios de ambas cámaras.

segments.src: Unless a meaningful number of Republicans join, a veto would likely stand.
segments.tr: A menos que un número significativo de republicanos se sume, es probable que el veto se mantenga.

segments.src: Tariff skepticism has existed in both parties and among many business groups, so cross-party coalitions are possible, but they are not guaranteed.
segments.tr: El escepticismo sobre los aranceles ha existido en ambos partidos y entre muchos grupos empresariales, por lo que las coaliciones entre partidos son posibles, pero no están garantizadas.

segments.src: Courts also matter.
segments.tr: Los tribunales también importan.

segments.src: Judicial rulings on how far presidential tariff authority extends can reshape the debate regardless of who controls Congress.
segments.tr: Los fallos judiciales sobre hasta dónde se extiende la autoridad arancelaria presidencial pueden reconfigurar el debate independientemente de quién controle el Congreso.

segments.src: ## The budget: where the "power of the purse" becomes real
segments.tr: ## El presupuesto: donde el "poder del monedero" se hace realidad

segments.src: Congress's strongest tool is funding.
segments.tr: La herramienta más sólida del Congreso es la financiación.

segments.src: Federal agencies operate on annual appropriations, and the fiscal year begins October 1.
segments.tr: Las agencias federales operan con asignaciones anuales, y el año fiscal comienza el 1 de octubre.

segments.src: A new majority gains leverage in several ways:
segments.tr: Una nueva mayoría gana influencia de varias maneras:

segments.src: - **Appropriations bills.** The House originates spending bills, and the Senate must also pass them. A majority in both chambers lets Democrats shape priorities, set funding levels and add policy guardrails.
segments.tr: - **Proyectos de ley de asignaciones.** La Cámara de Representantes origina los proyectos de ley de gasto y el Senado también debe aprobarlos. Una mayoría en ambas cámaras permite a los demócratas definir prioridades, fijar niveles de financiación y añadir salvaguardas políticas.

segments.src: - **Shutdown brinkmanship.** If the two branches cannot agree, funding lapses. Shutdowns are costly and politically risky for everyone involved, which is why most fights end in compromise.
segments.tr: - **Estrategias al borde del cierre del gobierno.** Si las dos ramas no se ponen de acuerdo, la financiación vence. Los cierres del gobierno son costosos y políticamente arriesgados para todos los involucrados, razón por la cual la mayoría de las disputas terminan en compromisos.

segments.src: - **Continuing resolutions and deadlines.** Short-term funding extensions often become the real negotiating moments.
segments.tr: - **Resoluciones de continuidad y plazos.** Las prórrogas de financiación a corto plazo a menudo se convierten en los verdaderos momentos de negociación.

segments.src: - **The debt limit.** Raising or suspending it is required to pay obligations already incurred, and it has repeatedly become a flashpoint.
segments.tr: - **El límite de la deuda.** Elevarlo o suspenderlo es necesario para pagar las obligaciones ya contraídas, y se ha convertido repetidamente en un punto de conflicto.

segments.src: The limits: the Senate filibuster still requires 60 votes for most legislation, unless the rules change.
segments.tr: Los límites: el filibusterismo del Senado sigue requiriendo 60 votos para la mayoría de las leyes, a menos que cambien las reglas.

segments.src: Any spending bill still needs the president's signature, so a final budget would be a negotiated outcome, not a one-party wish list.
segments.tr: Cualquier proyecto de ley de gasto sigue necesitando la firma del presidente, por lo que un presupuesto final sería el resultado de una negociación, no la lista de deseos de un solo partido.

segments.src: The president can also affect how funds are spent through administrative choices, which is a frequent source of disputes.
segments.tr: El presidente también puede influir en cómo se gastan los fondos a través de decisiones administrativas, lo cual es una fuente frecuente de disputas.

segments.src: ## Oversight: the quickest change you may notice
segments.tr: ## Supervisión: el cambio más rápido que podría notar

segments.src: The most immediate shift under a new majority is often not legislation but scrutiny.
segments.tr: El cambio más inmediato bajo una nueva mayoría a menudo no es la legislación, sino el escrutinio.

segments.src: Committee chairs control agendas, and they can:
segments.tr: Los presidentes de los comités controlan las agendas y pueden:

segments.src: - Schedule hearings and call witnesses
segments.tr: - Programar audiencias y citar a testigos

segments.src: - Issue subpoenas for documents and testimony
segments.tr: - Emitir citaciones para documentos y testimonios

segments.src: - Request audits and reports from watchdog agencies
segments.tr: - Solicitar auditorías e informes a las agencias de supervisión

segments.src: - Investigate agency decisions, contracts and spending
segments.tr: - Investigar decisiones, contratos y gastos de las agencias

segments.src: If the Senate also changes hands, the effects extend to **confirmations**.
segments.tr: Si el Senado también cambia de manos, los efectos se extienden a las **confirmaciones**.

segments.src: The Senate approves cabinet officials, judges and other senior appointments, so a different majority can slow, reshape or block nominations.
segments.tr: El Senado aprueba a los funcionarios del gabinete, jueces y otros cargos de alto nivel, por lo que una mayoría diferente puede frenar, modificar o bloquear los nombramientos.

segments.src: The House also holds the power to impeach, but conviction requires two-thirds of the Senate, a very high bar.
segments.tr: La Cámara de Representantes también tiene el poder de promover un juicio político (impeachment), pero la condena requiere dos tercios del Senado, un listón muy alto.

segments.src: Historically, impeachment has been rare and has not resulted in removal.
segments.tr: Históricamente, el juicio político ha sido raro y no ha derivado en la destitución del cargo.

segments.src: ## Reality check: divided government is still divided
segments.tr: ## Control de realidad: un gobierno dividido sigue estando dividido

segments.src: Even if both chambers flip, Washington would remain a system of shared power.
segments.tr: Incluso si ambas cámaras cambian de bando, Washington seguirá siendo un sistema de poder compartido.

segments.src: A president of the other party retains the veto, executive orders, enforcement discretion and the ability to direct agencies.
segments.tr: Un presidente del otro partido conserva el veto, las órdenes ejecutivas, la discrecionalidad en el cumplimiento de las leyes y la capacidad de dirigir las agencias.

segments.src: Expect:
segments.tr: Espere:

segments.src: - **Gridlock on major bills**, with compromise limited to must-pass items such as funding.
segments.tr: - **Parálisis legislativa en proyectos de ley importantes**, con acuerdos limitados a asuntos de aprobación obligatoria como la financiación.

segments.src: - **A heavy calendar of hearings** and investigations.
segments.tr: - **Un calendario cargado de audiencias** e investigaciones.

segments.src: - **Messaging votes** designed to frame choices ahead of 2028.
segments.tr: - **Votaciones con fines de posicionamiento político** diseñadas para definir opciones de cara a 2028.

segments.src: - **Court battles** over the boundaries of executive and legislative authority.
segments.tr: - **Batallas judiciales** sobre los límites de la autoridad ejecutiva y legislativa.

segments.src: ## What to watch before 2028
segments.tr: ## A qué prestar atención antes de 2028

segments.src: - **Certified results and final margins.** Narrow majorities make party discipline and absences matter.
segments.tr: - **Resultados certificados y márgenes finales.** Las mayorías estrechas hacen que la disciplina de partido y las ausencias cobren gran importancia.

segments.src: - **The next funding deadline.** It is the first big test of how the two branches work together.
segments.tr: - **El próximo plazo de financiación.** Es la primera gran prueba de cómo colaborarán las dos ramas del gobierno.

segments.src: - **Tariff developments.** Look for court decisions, trade negotiations and any bipartisan bills.
segments.tr: - **Evolución de los aranceles.** Esté atento a las resoluciones judiciales, las negociaciones comerciales y cualquier proyecto de ley bipartidista.

segments.src: - **Economic data.** Monthly inflation reports, wage growth and Fed decisions will shape the political mood more than any single vote.
segments.tr: - **Datos económicos.** Los informes mensuales de inflación, el crecimiento salarial y las decisiones de la Fed influirán en el clima político más que cualquier votación individual.

segments.src: - **Committee leadership.** Who chairs key panels signals which issues get priority.
segments.tr: - **Liderazgo de los comités.** Quién presida los paneles clave indicará qué temas tendrán prioridad.

segments.src: ## Bottom line
segments.tr: ## Conclusión

segments.src: A change in congressional control can reshape the agenda, the budget fights and the level of scrutiny in Washington.
segments.tr: Un cambio en el control del Congreso puede redefinir la agenda, las luchas presupuestarias y el nivel de escrutinio en Washington.

segments.src: It is much less likely to produce rapid, sweeping changes to prices or trade policy without cooperation from the White House.
segments.tr: Es mucho menos probable que produzca cambios rápidos y de gran alcance en los precios o en la política comercial sin la cooperación de la Casa Blanca.

segments.src: For readers, the practical takeaway is to watch what is passed and signed into law, and not only what is debated.
segments.tr: Para los lectores, la lección práctica es observar lo que se aprueba y se promulga como ley, y no solo lo que se debate.

us-20261123-news-2.title: 165.000 empleos y un 4,1% de desempleo: por qué un sólido informe de octubre no es una buena noticia para todos

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *This article is for general information only.

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## What the headline numbers say

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: A few points of context help:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: Pay is the second half of the story.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: Averages also hide differences.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: That has two effects:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: The reason is interest rates.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Here is how that chain usually works:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## What to watch next

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: These indicators give a fuller view:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## The bottom line

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.

us-20261123-news-3.title: ¿De recortes de tasas a subidas de tasas? Por qué algunos analistas ahora prevén un aumento de la Fed en 2027

segments.src: For much of the past two years, the main question about Federal Reserve policy was how fast and how far rates would fall.
segments.tr: Durante gran parte de los últimos dos años, la pregunta principal sobre la política de la Reserva Federal era qué tan rápido y qué tanto caerían las tasas.

segments.src: After a hotter-than-expected inflation report, a few forecasters are asking a different question: could the next move be up?
segments.tr: Tras un informe de inflación más alto de lo esperado, algunos pronosticadores se hacen una pregunta diferente: ¿podría ser el próximo movimiento al alza?

segments.src: Deutsche Bank is among the institutions that have reportedly shifted from expecting cuts to expecting a hike in 2027.
segments.tr: Deutsche Bank se encuentra entre las instituciones que, según se informa, han pasado de esperar recortes a esperar una subida en 2027.

segments.src: This is still a minority view.
segments.tr: Esta sigue siendo una opinión minoritaria.

segments.src: Here is what would have to happen for it to come true, and how it could affect household finances.
segments.tr: Aquí se explica lo que tendría que suceder para que esto se haga realidad y cómo podría afectar las finanzas de los hogares.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *Este artículo es solo para información general.

segments.src: It is not investment, tax or financial advice, and forecasts can be wrong.*
segments.tr: No constituye asesoramiento de inversión, fiscal o financiero, y los pronósticos pueden ser erróneos.*

segments.src: ## What changed
segments.tr: ## Qué cambió

segments.src: Forecasts move when the data surprise.
segments.tr: Los pronósticos se mueven cuando los datos sorprenden.

segments.src: A hot inflation report can do three things at once:
segments.tr: Un informe de inflación alto puede hacer tres cosas a la vez:

segments.src: - **Cut the odds of near-term easing.** If prices rise faster than expected, officials have less room to lower rates.
segments.tr: - **Reducir las probabilidades de una flexibilización a corto plazo.** Si los precios suben más rápido de lo esperado, los funcionarios tienen menos margen para bajar las tasas.

segments.src: - **Raise doubts about the path back to 2%.** One report rarely settles the trend, but several in a row can change how forecasters see the inflation outlook.
segments.tr: - **Generar dudas sobre el camino de regreso al 2%.** Un informe rara vez determina la tendencia, pero varios seguidos pueden cambiar la forma en que los pronosticadores ven las perspectivas de inflación.

segments.src: - **Shift market pricing.** Futures markets react quickly. Yields on shorter-term Treasuries often rise when traders push back or remove expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **Cambiar la valoración del mercado.** Los mercados de futuros reaccionan rápidamente. Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a corto plazo a menudo suben cuando los operadores posponen o eliminan los recortes esperados.

segments.src: Analysts who now see a hike are not saying it is certain.
segments.tr: Los analistas que ahora ven una subida no dicen que sea seguro.

segments.src: They are saying the risks have tilted toward tighter policy, and that is a notable change from a baseline of gradual easing.
segments.tr: Dicen que los riesgos se han inclinado hacia una política más restrictiva, y ese es un cambio notable respecto a una base de flexibilización gradual.

segments.src: ## What would have to happen for a hike
segments.tr: ## Qué tendría que suceder para una subida

segments.src: The Fed describes its goals as maximum employment and stable prices, with a long-run inflation target of 2%.
segments.tr: La Fed describe sus objetivos como el máximo empleo y precios estables, con un objetivo de inflación a largo plazo del 2%.

segments.src: Several conditions would likely need to line up before officials raised rates.
segments.tr: Probablemente tendrían que alinearse varias condiciones antes de que los funcionarios subieran las tasas.

segments.src: 1. **Inflation stays sticky or re-accelerates.** The Fed pays close attention to core measures, which leave out food and energy, and to services inflation such as housing and insurance. Several months of firm readings would matter more than a single report.
segments.tr: 1. **La inflación se mantiene persistente o se vuelve a acelerar.** La Fed presta mucha atención a las medidas subyacentes, que excluyen alimentos y energía, y a la inflación de los servicios, como la vivienda y los seguros. Varios meses de lecturas firmes importarían más que un solo informe.

segments.src: 2. **Inflation expectations drift higher.** If households and businesses start to expect faster price growth, that can make inflation harder to bring down. Policymakers watch surveys and market-based measures for this.
segments.tr: 2. **Las expectativas de inflación aumentan.** Si los hogares y las empresas comienzan a esperar un crecimiento de precios más rápido, eso puede hacer que la inflación sea más difícil de reducir. Los responsables de la política monetaria observan encuestas y medidas basadas en el mercado para esto.

segments.src: 3. **The labor market stays solid.** A hike is far easier to justify if hiring and wage growth remain strong. A clear weakening in jobs would work against it.
segments.tr: 3. **El mercado laboral se mantiene sólido.** Una subida es mucho más fácil de justificar si la contratación y el crecimiento salarial siguen siendo fuertes. Un debilitamiento claro en el empleo actuaría en contra de ello.

segments.src: 4. **Policymakers reach consensus.** Rate decisions are made by the Federal Open Market Committee, a group of voting members. Many officials would have to agree that tightening is needed, and the Fed has long preferred to signal such a shift in advance.
segments.tr: 4. **Los responsables de la política monetaria llegan a un consenso.** Las decisiones sobre las tasas las toma el Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto, un grupo de miembros con derecho a voto. Muchos funcionarios tendrían que estar de acuerdo en que se necesita un endurecimiento, y la Fed ha preferido durante mucho tiempo señalar tal cambio con antelación.

segments.src: If growth slows sharply, if inflation cools, or if financial stress appears, the cut-or-hold scenarios become more likely again.
segments.tr: Si el crecimiento se desacelera bruscamente, si la inflación se enfría o si aparece estrés financiero, los escenarios de recorte o mantenimiento vuelven a ser más probables.

segments.src: ## Why 2027 and not sooner
segments.tr: ## Por qué 2027 y no antes

segments.src: Central banks usually move slowly after a long period of policy change.
segments.tr: Los bancos centrales suelen moverse lentamente después de un largo período de cambio de política.

segments.src: A forecast for 2027 implies analysts expect the Fed to hold rates for a while, wait to see whether price pressures fade, and act only if they do not.
segments.tr: Un pronóstico para 2027 implica que los analistas esperan que la Fed mantenga las tasas por un tiempo, espere a ver si las presiones sobre los precios disminuyen y actúe solo si no lo hacen.

segments.src: Forecasts that far out carry wide margins of error.
segments.tr: Los pronósticos a tan largo plazo conllevan amplios márgenes de error.

segments.src: Fiscal policy, trade policy, energy prices, productivity and changes in Fed leadership can all alter the picture.
segments.tr: La política fiscal, la política comercial, los precios de la energía, la productividad y los cambios en el liderazgo de la Fed pueden alterar el panorama.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for your money
segments.tr: ## Qué podría significar para su dinero

segments.src: None of this is guaranteed.
segments.tr: Nada de esto está garantizado.

segments.src: These are general patterns, not predictions for any individual.
segments.tr: Estos son patrones generales, no predicciones para ningún individuo.

segments.src: ### Mortgages
segments.tr: ### Hipotecas

segments.src: Mortgage rates do not follow the Fed's policy rate directly.
segments.tr: Las tasas hipotecarias no siguen directamente la tasa de política de la Fed.

segments.src: They tend to track longer-term yields, especially the 10-year Treasury, along with investor demand for mortgage-backed securities.
segments.tr: Tienden a seguir los rendimientos a más largo plazo, especialmente el Tesoro a 10 años, junto con la demanda de los inversores de valores respaldados por hipotecas.

segments.src: If markets begin to price in a higher-for-longer or rising-rate path, mortgage rates could stay elevated or drift up.
segments.tr: Si los mercados comienzan a valorar una trayectoria de tasas más altas por más tiempo o en aumento, las tasas hipotecarias podrían mantenerse elevadas o subir.

segments.src: Anyone shopping for a home loan may want to compare offers from several lenders and ask about rate locks.
segments.tr: Cualquiera que busque un préstamo hipotecario puede querer comparar ofertas de varios prestamistas y preguntar sobre los bloqueos de tasas.

segments.src: Adjustable-rate loans are more sensitive to policy changes than fixed-rate loans.
segments.tr: Los préstamos de tasa ajustable son más sensibles a los cambios de política que los préstamos de tasa fija.

segments.src: ### Savings yields
segments.tr: ### Rendimientos de ahorro

segments.src: Savers are the group that usually benefits when rates stop falling.
segments.tr: Los ahorradores son el grupo que generalmente se beneficia cuando las tasas dejan de caer.

segments.src: Yields on high-yield savings accounts, money market funds and certificates of deposit generally follow short-term rates.
segments.tr: Los rendimientos de las cuentas de ahorro de alto rendimiento, los fondos del mercado monetario y los certificados de depósito generalmente siguen las tasas a corto plazo.

segments.src: If cuts are taken off the table, yields may stay near current levels longer than expected.
segments.tr: Si se descartan los recortes, los rendimientos pueden mantenerse cerca de los niveles actuales más tiempo de lo esperado.

segments.src: If hikes arrive, they could rise.
segments.tr: Si llegan las subidas, podrían aumentar.

segments.src: Banks adjust at different speeds, so it helps to compare rates and check whether an advertised rate is promotional.
segments.tr: Los bancos se ajustan a diferentes velocidades, por lo que es útil comparar tasas y verificar si una tasa anunciada es promocional.

segments.src: Also confirm that deposits are held at institutions covered by FDIC or NCUA insurance, within the coverage limits.
segments.tr: También confirme que los depósitos se mantengan en instituciones cubiertas por el seguro de la FDIC o NCUA, dentro de los límites de cobertura.

segments.src: ### Credit card rates
segments.tr: ### Tasas de tarjetas de crédito

segments.src: Most credit cards carry variable rates tied to the prime rate, which moves with the Fed's target range.
segments.tr: La mayoría de las tarjetas de crédito tienen tasas variables vinculadas a la tasa preferencial, que se mueve con el rango objetivo de la Fed.

segments.src: When the Fed raises rates, card APRs typically rise within a billing cycle or two.
segments.tr: Cuando la Fed sube las tasas, las TAE de las tarjetas generalmente aumentan dentro de uno o dos ciclos de facturación.

segments.src: When the Fed holds, card rates stay where they are, and they are already high for many borrowers.
segments.tr: Cuando la Fed mantiene, las tasas de las tarjetas se mantienen donde están, y ya son altas para muchos prestatarios.

segments.src: Anyone carrying a balance may want to look into paying it down, comparing lower-rate options, or reading the terms of any balance-transfer offer, including fees.
segments.tr: Cualquiera que tenga un saldo puede querer considerar pagarlo, comparar opciones de tasas más bajas o leer los términos de cualquier oferta de transferencia de saldo, incluidas las tarifas.

segments.src: ### Other loans
segments.tr: ### Otros préstamos

segments.src: Auto loans, personal loans, home equity lines of credit and some student loans can also be sensitive to rate changes, depending on whether the rate is fixed or variable.
segments.tr: Los préstamos para automóviles, préstamos personales, líneas de crédito sobre el valor de la vivienda y algunos préstamos estudiantiles también pueden ser sensibles a los cambios en las tasas, dependiendo de si la tasa es fija o variable.

segments.src: ## How to read forecasts like this
segments.tr: ## Cómo leer pronósticos como este

segments.src: - **Treat any single forecast as one view.** Banks and research firms often disagree, and their calls change when new data arrive.
segments.tr: - **Trate cualquier pronóstico individual como una opinión.** Los bancos y las firmas de investigación a menudo no están de acuerdo, y sus llamadas cambian cuando llegan nuevos datos.

segments.src: - **Watch the data the Fed watches.** Monthly inflation reports, employment data and the Fed's own projections give a clearer picture than headlines.
segments.tr: - **Observe los datos que observa la Fed.** Los informes mensuales de inflación, los datos de empleo y las propias proyecciones de la Fed ofrecen una imagen más clara que los titulares.

segments.src: - **Plan for a range of outcomes.** Households with flexible budgets, an emergency fund and manageable variable-rate debt are better placed whichever way rates go.
segments.tr: - **Planifique para una variedad de resultados.** Los hogares con presupuestos flexibles, un fondo de emergencia y una deuda de tasa variable manejable están mejor posicionados independientemente de hacia dónde vayan las tasas.

segments.src: - **Look at the source.** Official Fed statements and minutes are the best guide to what policymakers are actually thinking.
segments.tr: - **Mire la fuente.** Las declaraciones y actas oficiales de la Fed son la mejor guía de lo que realmente piensan los responsables de la política monetaria.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## La conclusión

segments.src: A hot inflation report has led some analysts to move from expecting rate cuts to expecting a hike in 2027.
segments.tr: Un informe de inflación alto ha llevado a algunos analistas a pasar de esperar recortes de tasas a esperar una subida en 2027.

segments.src: Whether that happens depends on whether inflation proves stubborn, whether expectations stay anchored and whether the job market holds up.
segments.tr: Si eso sucede depende de si la inflación resulta persistente, si las expectativas se mantienen ancladas y si el mercado laboral se mantiene.

segments.src: For households, the practical point is that borrowing costs may stay higher for longer than many had hoped.
segments.tr: Para los hogares, el punto práctico es que los costos de endeudamiento pueden mantenerse más altos por más tiempo de lo que muchos esperaban.

segments.src: Savers may keep earning solid yields, and variable-rate debt deserves attention.
segments.tr: Los ahorradores pueden seguir obteniendo rendimientos sólidos, y la deuda de tasa variable merece atención.

segments.src: Reviewing your own balance sheet is more useful than betting on any one forecast.
segments.tr: Revisar su propio balance es más útil que apostar por cualquier pronóstico.

segments.src: *Information in this article reflects general market commentary and may change.
segments.tr: *La información en este artículo refleja comentarios generales del mercado y puede cambiar.

segments.src: Consult a qualified financial professional before making decisions about your own finances.*
segments.tr: Consulte a un profesional financiero calificado antes de tomar decisiones sobre sus propias finanzas.*
